ctx.x: No, but we were almost like relatives. I'd be at his house all the time. Yeah.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: And his wife practically helped my mother to bring me up because that's how close-knit all families were here.

ctx.x: Well, who did you listen to come?

Well, Manuel Perez lived across the street from my grandfather, and he was part of the family. And there was another old trumpet player that I very seldom hear too much said about, George Moret. And his wife practically helped my mother to bring me up because that's how close-knit all families were here. All of the Creole families down in this area, they're close-knit. And half the time, my mother couldn't find me. I was either at Old Man Jaws Bowl by my grandfather, by Manuel Perez, all over to Bonnie's house,…
Were you any kind of Moret or Parade?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: when George would take me on the jobs with him, I was only in the area of a lot of ten, twelve years old.

ctx.x: Back to New Orleans in the early days, what did George Moret sound like?

George Moret was a rough, well, I'll explain it in musical terms, a rough trumpet player. Very good musician. Old man George Moret lived about three or four blocks from my house in the family. Real close friends through my grandfather and my father. And George could read music and actually he came from the old school or the old professors too. But he was loud and rough, if I can recall real well. Because when I went to, when George would take me on the jobs with him, I was only in the area of a lot of ten, twelve…
Do you remember him as playing any jazz or remember him as a brass band? Well, yes.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Yes, I used to go and stay at his house with his wife and his daughter. They used to consider me, as they called me, a play son.

ctx.x: You remember, were you still in New Orleans when Mr. Moret died? I don't know anything about him.

Yes, I was a little fellow. He's been dead then a long time. Oh, years and years. Yes, I used to go and stay at his house with his wife and his daughter. They used to consider me, as they called me, a play son.
Yes, we know nothing at all about him, his life, the facts of how old he was. Did he usually lead his own band?
